Effects of Estrogen: Estrogen is one of the main hormones regulating the menstrual cycle. During menstruation, the level of estrogen is too low to maintain the endometrium, causing its functional layer to shed.
Effects of Progesterone: Progestrone is a hormone which regulates the menstrual cycle by thickening the uterine lining, preparing for potential pregnancy. The level of progesterone is too low to maintain the endometrium stable, causing it to shed.
Effects of FSH: Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH) is a crucial hormone in stimulating egg development. During menstruation, the level of FSH is low but rising because GnRH is released by the hypothalamus, triggering the production of FSH by the anterior pituitary. This stimulates the development of several ovarian follicles.
Effects of LH: The level of the Luteinizing Hormone (LH) is low during menstruation but increases gradually as the hypothalamus releases GnRH, which triggers the anterior pituitary to release LH.
Energy Levels Info: You might be experiencing low energy and tiredness. This time calls for rest, recovery and gentle exercises.
What to eat: Eat foods containing iron to prevent  anemia and eat foods with vitamin B to provide energy. Some examples of foods to eat are red meat, poultry, fish, legumes,nuts and seeds and leafy greens.
Foods and Recipes: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here.
Concentration: Through this phase you might feel a difference on how well you can process information, as well as having harder time memorizing and lower attention. This is due to the lower amounts of estrogen levels.
Health: The average menstrual phase is 5 days, however this can vary depending on the person. This variation may alter the length of your menstrual cycle. If your overall cycle is longer than 35 days that can be a sign of  or shorter than 21 days. If you have concerns, contact your doctor.
Mood: During this time you might feel low and easily irritable. As well as feeling the need for more comfort than usual.
Types of Vitamins: While on your period you can take iron supplements to make up for the iron lost in blood and to prevent fatigue. Magnesium can be taken to support your muscles and also lower fatigue. Additionally Vitamin C can be taken to support iron absorption for inflammation and fatigue prevention. Before taking any supplements, please contact your doctor.
Insights in the Brain: The hypothalamus releases GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone), which stimulates the anterior pituitary to produce FSH and LH.
Insights in the Ovaries: A rising level of the Follicular Stimulating Hormone (FSH) stimulates the development of several ovarian follicles. No dominant follicle is yet observable, they are all competing.
Insights in the Uterus: The low amount of estrogen and progesterone cannot maintain the stability of the endometrium anymore, causing the uterine lining to shed blood and tissues: this is the menstrual flow.
Phase Info: It is the start of a new menstrual cycle. The body re-prepares itself for a future possible fertilization : the lining of the uterus is shed through the vagina and ovarian follicles start their development.
Today's Recap: Today you may feel tired, and low in energy. You might have a harder time concentrating and may experience a low and irritable mood.
